ratings.comment: Was a fine professor - main flaw as people have said is that his tests are very detail oriented and less on more important themes. Very doable as long as you go to class and study consistently instead of right before. Accessible for office hours.

He's really not that bad. His exams are all memorization-based (and all lecture-based too). If you know what to study, which is all the slides, then his exams aren't super difficult. Sometimes he mixes up the terms he's using which can be annoying.

Fantastic professor; a good lecturer and very passionate. 508 is a difficult class and he writes the toughest test out of the three professors, but he teaches in a way that forces you to really understand the material rather than just memorizing it. He is very accessible and helpful outside of class and clearly cares about student success.

Gives engaging and stimulating lectures and is always enthusiastic about the material, presenting it in a way that makes sense and is easy to follow. Also really great at answering student questions and clarifying things. Sometimes he gets a bit behind in lecture, but overall a great prof. for teaching 508.

Sebastian lectures like he's giving a Ted talk and tries too hard to be dramatic. His slow pace will get you 3 lectures behind and mess your lecture notes up. I did well on the tests, but they were brutal. Memorizing words from the slides were more important than the learning to do good on the exams. COVID-19 is saving my grade on the final.

His exams dont make sense. He asks you about random facts rather than concepts. He also has extremely wordy questions with a bunch of useless information. Horrible at writing test questions and cant seem to stick to the lecture schedule like his colleagues. Makes it difficult to keep track of where we are in the course

Sebastian was a fine professor, but I felt that his tests relied a bit too heavily on irrelevant details rather than useful concepts. Get ready to memorize names of enzymes and cofactors. While I preferred the other professors in the course, it is certainly possible to succeed in his section, just put in the time.
Bednarek is a passionate professor, but unfortunately, he's not a good one. The exams are more a trivia test than a knowledge test.

Professor Bednarek was the worst professor I have had at UW-Madison. I really enjoy biochemistry and found the information very interesting. I was killing it in the class for the first 2 professors, but my grade dropped from an A to a B after Bednarek took over. I had a deep understanding of every slide he posted, but it meant nothing for the final

He has a bad rap for some reason, not really sure why.  He is a great lecturer who is clearly very enthusiastic about biochemistry and wants to share his knowledge with his students.  Unfortunately he isn't always the most helpful, especially in office hours, and his exams are tough but not impossible, he makes you work for it but you learn a lot.

Professor Bednarek is a super nice guy, and really tries to help his students learn biochem. Unfortunately he's absolutely horrible at it. I went into the final with an A, and lost it coming out. I studied for his exams the exact same way that I did for all of other units (which I got A's on), and found them to be very confusing, and poorly worded.

Avoid at all costs. Confusing lectures that ramble on, trick questions both in in-class activities and exams, and insufficient explanations in lectures. For a class that is already challenging enough, his teaching style makes it near impossible and he has a tendency to push detail towards grad-level. Unfortunately there are no other options for 508

He's that kid who didn't read more than the first 30 pages of assigned readings, so all of his suggestions for class discussion questions are extrapolations of minutiae. That is to say his exams will not test any conceptual understanding of biochemistry, but that's par for the course with 507/508. Singlehandedly ruined my chances of an A in 508.

Neither his lectures nor his lecture slides are clear. I love biochemistry but this professor made it impossible to enjoy the class. I had to read and learn things from other sources. I had taken many genetics classes before this but he finds some too specific things that should be learned in other classes like molecular bio or genetics.

A pretty average professor, honestly. He takes forever to get through each slide and he never finishes his lectures on time. Often repeats himself. He does a good job of explaining though...eventually. Tests aren't too bad. Actually writes out text on slides, which is great. Just read his PPT's don't listen to the lectures.

Everything is relative and relative to Cox, Nelson, and Pagliarini, he is simply not good.  For some reason, it takes him forever to reach a point.  The way he talks is extremely slow and laborious.  If he lectured using Dave Nelson's slides he would take three class periods to complete one lecture.   Boom roasted.
I thought prof bednarek was great! He was really interested in the students and his exams fairly represented what he taught. He was my favorite 508 prof

cannot stay on topic. repeats himself frequently and never finishes all of the material for the lecture. exam material often not in his lecture notes.  if you can, take classes from other biochem profs.
gets off track really easily, this is a hard class due to the huge amount of memorization,the stuff he goes over in class insn't that useful for exams but lectures are sort of interesting.

Most frustrating prof ever. Continually asks redundant questions (to which the answers are often the title of the ppt slide behind him). Frequently misspeaks, has never finished a whole lecture, wastes time repeating himself. I love biochem but can't stand his class.  SHOULD NOT BE ALLOWED TO TEACH 508
